title: Conformance: integrate shared runner + add CI job for cross-SDK client behavior scenarios
author: Leila Farouk
release_notes: Internal-only: adds conformance test runner integration and CI gating job (no SDK API changes).
body:
Context: As part of the SDK parity audit, we’re adding a conformance harness that can be executed across Python/TS/Go to prevent regressions in auth/retry/timeout/streaming behavior. This PR wires the shared conformance runner into the Python SDK repo, adds an initial scenario set (focused on retry/timeouts/error taxonomy), and adds a dedicated CI job so conformance is enforced on every PR.

What’s included (Python repo):
- Conformance runner integration:
  - Adds a lightweight adapter that exposes the Python client via a stable interface (create client, send request, collect structured result).
  - Normalizes output into a JSON-ish result object that the runner can diff/validate (status, error_type, attempts, timings, observed_headers).
- Initial scenario set (shared across SDKs):
  - retry/429_respects_retry_after: verifies Retry-After is honored (bounded) and backoff includes jitter.
  - retry/503_flap_budgeted: verifies retry budget is enforced (no infinite loops), surfaces RetryExhausted with classifier info.
  - timeout/non_stream_overall_timeout: verifies overall timeout maps to TimeoutError (not a generic Exception) with consistent message.
  - headers/request_id_propagation: verifies request-id is captured from response headers and included in error metadata when present.
  - errors/transport_reset_retryable: verifies a simulated connection reset is retryable and counted.
- CI job:
  - Adds a “conformance” job to GitHub Actions that runs on ubuntu-latest with pinned Python.
  - Uses a local mocked gateway (http server) started as part of the test step; no external network calls.
  - Uploads conformance artifacts on failure (runner logs + scenario report) to speed up debugging.
- Flake mitigation:
  - Hard caps on per-scenario runtime and retries.
  - Fixed ports avoided (bind to ephemeral); runner passes the chosen port to the client.
  - Time-based assertions are bounded and avoid tight timing expectations.

How to run locally:
- make conformance (recommended)
- Or: python -m pytest tests/conformance -k conformance

Notes / follow-ups:
- This PR only adds the harness + initial scenarios; it does not change the SDK retry/timeout implementations themselves (those land in PRs 412/413/415).
- We’re tracking known CI flake sources in INT-441; this PR adds artifact uploads and removes fixed-port assumptions.

Screenshots/log snippets:
- Example failing report (truncated):
  - scenario: retry/429_respects_retry_after
  - expected: attempts<=4, observed_attempts=7
  - expected: retry_after_applied=true
  - observed: retry_after_applied=false

This should give us a stable baseline to align TS/Go against and to keep parity from regressing as we ship the new defaults.
commits: test(conformance): add python adapter and result normalization
test(conformance): add initial scenario manifests + pytest wrappers
ci: add conformance workflow job and artifact upload on failure
chore: docs for running conformance locally
checks: CI Summary: build (pass); unit-tests (pass); lint (pass); conformance (pass, 5 scenarios); packaging (pass). Reruns: conformance rerun once on Feb 1 due to port bind issue; fixed by binding to ephemeral port + passing through runner config.
conversation:
Ibrahim Khan (review): Can we guarantee these tests don’t hit the public gateway? We can’t have PR CI depend on external network. Also, please document where scenario definitions live and how TS/Go will consume the same fixtures.

Leila Farouk (author): Yep—runner spins up a local mocked gateway server (no outbound calls). Added a guard that fails the run if base_url is not localhost/127.0.0.1. Added tests/conformance/README.md describing fixture layout and the cross-SDK contract.

Sahana Iyer (review): CI: please make the conformance job upload artifacts on failure; also ensure it doesn’t run in parallel with itself in a way that shares ports. We’ve had flakes in INT-441.

Leila Farouk (author): Added artifact upload (scenario report + logs). Removed fixed ports and bind to :0; runner passes port to client adapter. Also added per-scenario hard timeouts.

Rafael Mendes (review): Retry scenarios: avoid strict timing assertions; CI runners are noisy. Prefer attempt counts + bounds and ensure Retry-After is bounded. Also ensure we’re not asserting jitter distribution.

Leila Farouk (author): Updated scenarios to assert: attempt_count <= max_attempts, retry_after_applied=true, and total_sleep_ms within [min,max] envelope. No jitter distribution assertions.

Ibrahim Khan (final): Looks good. This gives us a baseline to hold Python/TS/Go to. Approved.

Merged by Leila Farouk via squash after CI green.
